turns.user: Hollow cylinder, 300 mm diameter, 500 mm tall, 20 mm nozzle, 10 mm layers, 20 s per layer. Fresh density 2150 kg/m3, static yield stress 1.2 kPa, Athix 0.5 Pa/s. Will it stand?
turns.text:
I’ll check the buildability tool using the geometry, cycle time, and fresh-state values you supplied. I’ll state any geometry assumptions the calculator requires.
**No.** The calculator predicts plastic collapse around layer 11 of 50, at a height of about **107 mm**. The main shortfall is the **20 s layer cycle**: at that cycle time, it estimates you would need either an initial static yield stress of about **8.63 kPa** or a structuration rate of about **7.93 Pa/s**.

With your measured values, the estimated stable cycle time starts at about **317 s per layer** (about **5.3 minutes**), assuming the calculator’s default bead width of **23.69 mm**—1.2 times the nozzle diameter. That is a modeled schedule estimate; the actual print still needs experimental verification.
